articles.title_original: Flow-Induced Structuring of Polypropylene-Based Composites for Improved Mechanical and Thermal Performance
articles.title_en: Flow Alignment Boosts Thermal Conductivity of PP/BN Composites
articles.excerpt_original: Polypropylene (PP)/hexagonal boron nitride (BN) composites were formulated through melt compounding and subsequently subjected to non-isothermal uniaxial elongational flow to assess how flow-induced microstructural evolution governs mechanical and thermal performance. Rheological characterization of the isotropic, as-compounded materials revealed increasing melt elasticity with BN loading. At 25 wt% BN, a pseudo-solid-like response emerged, suggesting the development of an incipient interconnected filler structure. In the isotropic state, BN increased stiffness, tensile strength, and thermal conductivity, with only minor effects on PP crystallinity. The application of the non-isothermal elongational flow further improved the mechanical response, particularly at high BN loading, indicating an additional contribution from flow-induced reorganization of the filler phase. X-ray diffraction confirmed the preferential alignment of BN platelets along the fiber direction. This structural reorganization was accompanied by an increase in thermal conductivity of approximately 56% for PP containing 25 wt% BN. Overall, the obtained results demonstrate that non-isothermal elongational flow can effectively tailor BN orientation and polymer-chain organization, providing a solvent-free and scalable route to enhance the mechanical and thermal performance of PP/BN composites.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that non-isothermal elongational flow aligns boron nitride platelets in polypropylene composites, improving mechanical performance and increasing thermal conductivity by about 56% at 25 wt% BN. The solvent-free process offers a scalable route for tailoring thermally conductive polymer composites.

articles.title_original: Tribology at the Flip of a Switch: Dynamic Control of Friction and Adhesion with Surface Phonon Polaritons
articles.title_en: Light-Controlled Friction and Adhesion Using Surface Phonon Polaritons
articles.excerpt_original: Advanced applications of robotics and haptics require the ability to modulate friction and adhesion in a dynamic fashion, in real time. Existing technologies, however, suffer from the need for high voltage circuitry, slow response times, and poor spatial resolution, limiting their utility. Moving away from traditional approaches, here we demonstrate that tuned interfacial interactions involving surface phonon polaritons (SPhPs) can control friction and adhesion in real time at surfaces. SPhPs are hybrid light-matter states formed by the coupling of photons and phonons, which can be excited in polar dielectrics. Since phonon coupling is a primary mechanism for frictional energy dissipation, optically gating SPhPs provides a pathway to controlling this. Moreover, the dipolar nature of the polaritons can modify adhesion in response to localized surface electric field confinement. Here, using atomic force microcopy (AFM), we demonstrate that when SiC thin films are optically pumped in the Reststrahlen (RS) band, the friction and adhesion between a Pt probe tip and a SiC surface can be turned “on” and “off’ with light, with a nearly 3-fold increase in friction and 4-fold increase in adhesion, when illuminated. The influence of SiC film thickness, local interfacial dielectric, and optical excitation energy are described.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated reversible, real-time control of friction and adhesion at a silicon carbide surface by optically exciting surface phonon polaritons. AFM measurements showed nearly threefold higher friction and fourfold higher adhesion under illumination, indicating potential for haptics and robotic interfaces without conventional high-voltage actuation.

articles.title_original: Band gap modulation via interlayer twist angle in semiconductor hydrogenated borophene
articles.title_en: Twist angle modulates band gaps in hydrogenated borophene bilayers
articles.excerpt_original: Borophene is a compelling 2D material known for its considerable structural diversity, and its lack of a band gap can be overcome by synthesis of hydrogenated borophene, also known as borophane. However, with the realization of semiconductor borophane polymorphs, understanding the mechanisms controlling their band gaps is fundamental, particularly in vertically stacked architectures, where the role of interlayer coupling must be fully elucidated. Here, we investigate the electronic properties of semiconductor borophane bilayers in different stacking arrangements using density functional theory calculations. Our results show weak interlayer binding, with minor effects on bond lengths, low exfoliation energies, and little charge redistribution. In contrast, interlayer coupling of electron states plays an important role in band gaps, mainly by modifying the conduction bands, an effect strongly influenced by the stacking configuration. The linear optical response also depends on the interlayer twist angle and is strongly affected by excitonic effects in this material. These findings establish a fundamental framework for band gap engineering in borophene-based architectures, paving the way for their integration into next-generation nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.
articles.summary_en: Density functional theory shows that interlayer coupling in semiconductor borophane bilayers substantially affects band gaps, primarily by modifying conduction bands. Stacking configuration and twist angle also influence optical response, supporting band-gap engineering for future nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.

articles.title_original: Charge-conserving creation and annihilation of topological phase singularities in atomically thin semiconductors
articles.title_en: MoS₂ Study Demonstrates Charge-Conserving Optical Phase Singularities
articles.excerpt_original: Atomically thin transition metal dichalcogenides provide a promising material platform for optical phase manipulation, as rapid variations in their dielectric functions can give rise to topological phase singularities (PSs). However, PS evolution while preserving topological charge conservation has not yet been investigated in exciton enabled PS systems. Here, using atomically thin MoS2 films on sapphire as a model system, we theoretically and experimentally demonstrate that the evolution of dielectric dispersion determines the creation, trajectory, merging, and annihilation of optical PSs under topological charge conservation. By varying the MoS2 film thickness, we experimentally realize this evolution through the gradual shrinking of the high energy n-k dispersion loop, which modifies its intersection with the zero reflection condition. Our results provide a general strategy for exploring and manipulating topological optical states.
articles.summary_en: Researchers theoretically and experimentally show that atomically thin MoS₂ can support the creation, movement, merging, and annihilation of optical phase singularities while conserving topological charge. Thickness-dependent dielectric dispersion provides a strategy for manipulating topological optical states in semiconductor platforms.

articles.title_original: Group-IV semiconductor physics and technologies for next-generation electron-photon-spin integrated devices on silicon
articles.title_en: Group-IV Semiconductor Technologies for Integrated Electron–Photon–Spin Devices
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract This paper reviews group-IV semiconductor physics and technologies for realizing ultra-low-power electron-photon-spin semiconductor systems on a silicon platform. First, some technologies for high-speed CMOS and silicon photonics devices are introduced on the basis of heteroepitaxy of Ge, SiGe, and GeSn alloys on Si. Next, aiming to integrate logic and nonvolatile memory, electrical spin injection and detection technologies for spin transistors are explained using Ge on Si. Also, recent progress of the studies of spin-related physical properties such as spin relaxation time and spin diffusion length is introduced for Ge. Meanwhile, recent research progress on low-temperature-formed gate stack structures, Ge-on-Insulator (GOI) structures, and Ge/SiGe multi-heterostructures will be presented to combine CMOS technology with spintronic and/or spin-photonic devices on a Si platform. Finally, the possibilities of spin-tunnel FETs, vertical spin FETs, GeSn-based spin devices on the Si platform will be described for future applications.
articles.summary_en: This review examines Ge, SiGe, and GeSn technologies on silicon for integrating CMOS, photonic, spintronic, and spin-photonic functions. It covers heteroepitaxy, spin injection and detection, gate stacks, Ge-on-insulator structures, and emerging spin-FET architectures.

articles.title_original: Intrinsic i‐Wave Altermagnetism in 2D Graphene Superlattices
articles.title_en: Study proposes graphene platform for higher-order altermagnetic spintronics
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Altermagnets feature unconventional magnetism due to their momentum‐dependent spin splitting purely driven by magnetic order, for which a variety of transition‐metal‐based ‐wave altermagnets have been proposed. However, carbon‐based altermagnets remain largely unexplored, even though magnetism of graphene nanostructures has been widely demonstrated. Here, through a comprehensive symmetry analysis, we establish a symmetry‐guided design principle for realizing higher‐order ‐wave altermagnetism in graphene antidot superlattices and demonstrate its emergence in both monolayer and bilayer graphene, particularly in the Bernal‐stacked bilayer. By combining atomistic tight binding models and first principles methods, we show the appearance of an interaction‐induced ‐wave altermagnetic splitting, originating from the intrinsic magnetic instability of 2D graphene antidot superlattices. Our work establishes a strategy to engineer ‐wave altermagnetism in a graphene platform, extending the materials landscape beyond conventional ‐wave altermagnets and putting forward a carbon‐based platform for higher‐order altermagnetic spintronics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers use symmetry analysis, tight-binding models and first-principles methods to predict interaction-induced higher-order altermagnetism in monolayer and bilayer graphene antidot superlattices. The work offers a theoretical design strategy for carbon-based spintronic materials, particularly in Bernal-stacked bilayer graphene.

articles.title_original: Graphene powerline energy harvester powers a batteryless sensor
articles.title_en: Graphene Powerline Harvester Enables Batteryless Sensor Operation
articles.excerpt_original: Autonomous Internet of Things sensors require practical ways to obtain operating power from their surroundings. In this study, the authors crafted various two-dimensional spiral and three-dimensional helix graphene inductors. The inductance was characterized by measuring the current through the inductor as a function of both applied voltage and frequency. Next, the induced voltage and current produced inside the graphene inductor were measured as a function of the current flowing inside a nearby power cable. A single graphene inductor with an inner steel core can produce a voltage high enough to activate a Cockcroft–Walton (CW) circuit. The CW circuit passively rectifies the inductor signal and multiplies its amplitude. Different multiplier stages are used to charge three different storage capacitors up to the voltage levels required to operate a custom low-power-consuming temperature sensor system. The basic operation and performance of the sensor system are presented. Replacing the usual power-management chip and rechargeable battery with these storage capacitors lowered the sensor’s overall power consumption and extended its projected service life. The demonstrated sensor operates after a one-time stage in which the storage capacitors are initially charged and the CPU is programmed; autonomous cold-start operation was not evaluated.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed graphene spiral and helical inductors that harvest energy from nearby power cables and passively boost it to charge storage capacitors. The system powered a low-consumption temperature sensor without a battery, although autonomous cold-start operation was not demonstrated.

articles.title_original: Graphene-enhanced micro-flexible supercapacitor electrodes (D2.1)
articles.title_en: Graphene-Enhanced Printed Electrodes for Flexible Supercapacitors
articles.excerpt_original: This deliverable is purposed to report research within Task 2.1.a (WP2) on developing a suite of techniques to fabricate graphene-enhanced micro-flexible supercapacitor (SC) electrodes with increased power density, mechanical flexibility and long-term stability. The electrodes should also possess good combability with the atomic layer deposition (ALD) processing in WP3. Briefly, our techniques consist of ink formulation, printing, performance characterization, and ALD compatibility tests. The ink formulation step is to transfer the raw materials, activated carbon (AC), developed in WP1 to printable inks through two strategies, graphene-enriched AC inks stabilized by thermally stable polymeric binders and grapheneenabled binder-free AC inks. Both inks benefit from the presence of graphene and the printed electrode materials match the high-temperature ALD processing in WP3. The printing step involves the development of dedicated scalable printing processes, mainly including doctor blading and 3D printing (direct ink writing), to print the inks on flexible substrates. The performance characterization includes systematic characterization of the electric, electrochemical, and mechanic properties of the printed micro-flexible electrodes. The ALD combability tests are to evaluate the effects of ALD processing on the electrochemical and mechanical performance of the printed micro-flexible electrodes. The deliverable establishes techniques to transfer raw materials developed in WP1 to robust high-performance electrodes for the ALD processes in WP3.
articles.summary_en: The research develops graphene-enriched and binder-free activated-carbon inks for doctor-blade and 3D printing onto flexible substrates. It evaluates electrical, electrochemical, mechanical, and atomic-layer-deposition compatibility to support stable, high-power micro-flexible supercapacitor electrodes.

articles.title_original: Single-Asperity Sliding Behavior on Graphene Surface Modulated by Metal Substrate Doping: A DFT Study
articles.title_en: DFT Study Examines Metal-Substrate Effects on Graphene Sliding
articles.summary_en: An academic DFT study investigates how doping a metal substrate modulates single-asperity sliding behavior on graphene. The work provides fundamental insights into graphene–substrate tribology without indicating a specific commercial application.

articles.title_original: Broadband multi-functional graphene-MoS$$_2$$ polarization conversion metasurface for biomolecular refractive index sensing at the THz band
articles.title_en: Graphene–MoS₂ metasurface enables tunable THz biomolecular sensing
articles.excerpt_original: A tunable multifunctional reflective metasurface is proposed and numerically studied for mid-terahertz (THz) polarization conversion and refractive-index sensing. The unit cell comprises two orthogonally arranged elliptical resonators with rectangular cross-slots, integrated with a graphene layer, a MoS \(_2\) layer, a SiO \(_2\) spacer, and a gold ground plane. The electromagnetic characteristics of the structure are investigated using the frequency-domain finite-element method (FEM), with graphene and MoS \(_2\) described by the Kubo and Drude models, respectively. Owing to the hybrid graphene–MoS \(_2\) configuration, the metasurface supports dual-band linear-to-linear (LP-to-LP) polarization conversion in the ranges 1.233–1.409 THz and 2.172–2.215 THz, as well as broadband linear-to-circular (LP-to-CP) polarization conversion from 1.574 to 2.105 THz. The polarization-conversion performance remains high across the operating bands and is maintained for incident angles up to 45 \(^\circ\) . In addition, the proposed metasurface demonstrates high-performance refractive-index sensing capability through analyte-induced spectral resonance shifts. Across the biological refractive-index range ( \(n = 1.33\) –1.49), the sensor exhibits average sensitivities of 380.5 GHz/RIU and 748.2 GHz/RIU for the first and second resonance modes, respectively, reaching peak local sensitivities of up to 1.25 THz/RIU and 1.45 THz/RIU for high-index biological analytes. Furthermore, the device achieves maximum figure-of-merit (FOM) values of 6.41 RIU \(^{-1}\) and 6.04 RIU \(^{-1}\) , quality factors ranging from 6.6 to 10.8 (first resonance) and 9.2 to 15.4 (second resonance), and a minimum limit of detection (LOD) of 0.0078 RIU. articles.summary_en: Researchers numerically designed a graphene–MoS₂ metasurface that provides broadband THz polarization conversion and refractive-index sensing. The proposed device reaches sensitivities up to 1.45 THz/RIU and a minimum detection limit of 0.0078 RIU across biological analytes.

articles.title_original: MXene-Mediated Dynamic Redox Initiation for the Rapid Fabrication of Gelled Adhesive Conductive Hydrogels for Applications in Self-Powered Flexible Electronics
articles.title_en: MXene Hydrogel Enables Rapid-Fabricated Self-Powered Flexible Electronics
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Conductive hydrogels are promising soft materials for wearable electronics and self-powered sensing systems; however, their practical implementation is often limited by sluggish gelation kinetics, energy-intensive preparation processes, and insufficient integration of mechanical robustness, adhesion, and electrical functionality. Herein, we report a rapidly gelled MXene-reinforced adhesive conductive hydrogel, denoted as PAHM (PAA-PHEMA-MXene), constructed through a MXene/Fe3+/ammonium persulfate redox initiation strategy. The redox-active MXene nanosheets promote the decomposition of persulfate under ambient conditions, enabling fast free-radical polymerization of acrylic acid and hydroxyethyl methacrylate without an external energy input. Meanwhile, MXene nanosheets serve as multifunctional nanofillers and interfacial interaction sites, while Fe3+ coordination, hydrogen bonding, and gelatin association synergistically reinforce the polymer network. As a result, the PAHM hydrogel can be formed within 30 s and exhibits a tensile strength of 525 kPa, an elongation at break of 860%, good cyclic stability, and strong adhesion to diverse substrates, with a shear adhesion strength of 128 kPa on copper foil. Benefiting from its combined stretchability, adhesion, and conductivity, the hydrogel was further employed as a flexible electrode for a triboelectric nanogenerator. The resulting PAHM-TENG delivered an open-circuit voltage of 130 V at a contact frequency of 3 Hz, successfully powered 27 light-emitting diodes and a commercial calculator and maintained stable electrical output over 10800 cycles of continuous operation. In addition, the PAHM hydrogel showed rapid electromechanical response and potential for wearable motion monitoring. This work provides a facile ma
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a MXene-reinforced adhesive conductive hydrogel that gels within 30 seconds without external energy input. The material combines high stretchability, adhesion and conductivity, powering a triboelectric nanogenerator and supporting wearable motion monitoring.

articles.title_original: Defect Engineering, Interface Design, and Heterostructure Integration: Three Material-Level Strategies for Low-Energy Synaptic Weight Update in MoS₂-Based Two-Dimensional Memristors
articles.title_en: Graphene Interfaces Enable Ultra-Low-Energy MoS₂ Memristors
articles.excerpt_original: Practical artificial synapse operation relies on continuous conductance modulation, making electrical programming conditions decisive to device energy expenditure. In real synaptic updates, working voltage, operational current and pulse duration together determine energy consumption. This review compares three material-level engineering strategies for lowering the electrical cost of synaptic weight adjustment in MoS₂-based two-dimensional memristors: (1) argon-plasma defect engineering of monolayer MoS₂, (2) graphene-interface design in a graphene/MoS₂/SiOₓ/Ni stack, and (3) an all-2D van der Waals heterostructure combining MoS₂, h-BN and graphene. Under ten +20 V and ten −20 V, 1 ms potentiation/depression pulses, argon-plasma-treated monolayer MoS₂ (sulfur-vacancy density ≈3.4×10¹⁴ cm⁻²) reached a minimum programming energy of approximately 30 fJ per pulse and a switching ratio of 10⁴. Under 64 pulses of +4.5 V and 64 pulses of −3 V, each 50 μs wide, a graphene-barrier interface restricted the programming current to as low as 100 nA and produced a non-linearity factor of 0 in both potentiation and depression under that specific pulse condition, though linearity degraded when the pulse parameters or channel thickness changed. Under ±15 V, 40 ns pulses, an all-2D floating-gate heterostructure reached approximately 18 fJ per pulse across roughly 3,000 quasi-continuous conductance states. Together, these three strategies show that current suppression, carrier-injection barriers, and short-pulse tunnelling control are complementary, material-level routes to lowering the electrical cost of synaptic weight update, each trading differently against operating voltage, pulse duration and update linearity.
articles.summary_en: A review compares defect engineering, graphene-interface design, and MoS₂/h-BN/graphene heterostructures for reducing synaptic-update energy in two-dimensional memristors. Reported minimum energies reach approximately 30 fJ and 18 fJ per pulse, although performance depends on voltage, pulse duration, channel thickness, and update linearity.

articles.title_original: Electrochemical performance of BN – Me (Ti, Cr, Al, Zr) composite nanopowders synthesized under concentrated light with reduced surface-driven contributions
articles.title_en: BN–Metal Composite Nanopowders Show Tunable Acidic-Electrode Performance
articles.excerpt_original: BN–Ti, BN–Cr, BN–Al, and BN–Zr composite nanopowders were synthesized under concentrated light in nitrogen and tested as cathodically polarized electrodes in 0.1 M H₂SO₄. The ultrafast heating route produced structurally heterogeneous, partially oxidized composites, which were heat-treated at 400 °C to reduce surface-defect effects. XRD and Raman revealed amorphous/turbostratic BN domains with boron oxides (B₂O₃, H₃BO₃) and dispersed metal oxides (TiO₂, ZrO₂, Cr₂O₃, γ-Al₂O₃), without bulk nitride/boride phases. TEM showed additive-dependent architectures: BN–Cr formed fibrous networks of high surface area, while BN–Ti/Zr produced agglomerated nanoparticles. Electrochemically, BN–Cr delivered the highest instantaneous currents and earliest polarization onset, BN–Al the largest integrated charge via acid-induced restructuring of γ-Al₂O₃, and BN–Ti/Zr intermediate capacitive responses. Cycling confirmed BN’s stabilizing role, suppressing oxide dissolution and enabling beneficial surface reconstruction. These results establish BN–metal composites as durable, composition-tunable electrodes in acidic environments, with additive choice governing architecture, kinetics, and charge-storage behavior.
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized BN–Ti, BN–Cr, BN–Al, and BN–Zr nanopowders using concentrated light and evaluated them as cathodic electrodes in sulfuric acid. BN–Cr delivered the strongest instantaneous currents, while BN–Al provided the greatest integrated charge, indicating composition-dependent architectures and electrochemical behavior.

articles.title_original: Attosecond Quantum Optical Spectroscopy of Topological Materials
articles.title_en: Quantum-Light Spectroscopy Reveals Signatures of Topological Matter
articles.excerpt_original: High-harmonic generation (HHG) provides an ultrafast probe of quantum materials, yet conventional spectral observables do not generally furnish a common signature of band topology. Here we show that quantum-light-driven HHG opens an additional information channel through the photon statistics of the emitted harmonics. Using the Haldane Chern insulator and the time-reversal-invariant Kane-Mele topological insulator, we calculate helicity-resolved equal-time intensity correlations and identify a common enhancement of high-order harmonic correlations in the topological phases. For the Haldane model, a dichroic correlation constructed from opposite helicity channels reverses sign with the Chern number. These signatures originate from the distinct nonlinear response sampled by quantum fluctuations of the driving field and are absent from the corresponding mean harmonic spectra as a common classifier. Our results establish photon-correlation spectroscopy as a route to interrogate topological matter with quantum light and provide a bridge between strong-field solid-state physics and quantum optics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that photon statistics from high-harmonic generation can distinguish topological phases, overcoming limitations of conventional harmonic spectra. Helicity-resolved correlations also track the Chern number in the Haldane model, suggesting a new quantum-optical probe of topological materials.

articles.title_original: Two-Dimensional Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Transistors for Flexible Electronics: Progress, Interface Engineering and Reliability Challenges
articles.title_en: Review Assesses Progress and Reliability Challenges in Flexible TMD Transistors
articles.excerpt_original: Flexible electronic systems require semiconductor devices and materials that can provide reliable electrical performance while conforming to curved, moving, or deformable surfaces. Two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides, including MoS₂, WS₂, and WSe₂, are promising candidates because their atomically thin structures, semiconducting bandgaps, and mechanically compliant nature are suitable for low-power flexible transistors. This review critically examines how the material properties, fabrication methods, and interface engineering of these semiconductors influence their electrical performance, mechanical durability, and potential for large-scale integration. Recent advances are compared with selected foundational research to evaluate progress from individual field-effect transistors to wafer-scale arrays and functional flexible circuits. The reviewed evidence shows that substantial advances have been made in nanoscale channel fabrication, high-κ dielectric integration, and circuit complexity. However, the technological maturity of flexible TMD electronics remains limited by material non-uniformity, transfer-induced contamination, contact resistance, dielectric defects, unstable p-type behaviour, and insufficiently standardised reliability testing. High performance in selected devices therefore does not necessarily indicate reproducible manufacturing or long-term mechanical stability. Future research should prioritise defect-controlled wafer-scale growth, clean low-temperature integration, mechanically durable interfaces, complementary logic, and statistically meaningful bending tests. TMD transistors are unlikely to replace conventional silicon electronics in the immediate future, but they could complement silicon in transparent, wearable, and conformable low-po
articles.summary_en: A review finds that transition metal dichalcogenide transistors, including MoS₂, WS₂ and WSe₂, have advanced from individual devices toward wafer-scale arrays and flexible circuits. However, non-uniformity, contamination, contact resistance, dielectric defects and inadequate reliability testing continue to limit manufacturing readiness and long-term stability.

articles.title_original: Defect control via Cu enrichment enhances multifunctional properties in the polar semiconductor Cu 1 + x Mn 1 − y SiTe 3
articles.title_en: Cu Enrichment Reduces Defects and Enhances Polar Semiconductor Functions
articles.excerpt_original: Polar materials have recently attracted significant interest due to their rich multifunctional properties. The chalcogenide polar semiconductor Cu1-xMn1+ySiTe3 (Cu-deficient) is an emerging multiferroic system in which electric polarization is coupled to magnetization. However, its macroscopic ferroelectric polarization is strongly suppressed due to the presence of a high density of stacking faults. In this work, we demonstrate that these crystal defects, likely originating from non-stoichiometry, can be substantially reduced by increasing the Cu content. Cu-enriched samples, Cu1+xMn1-ySiTe3, crystallize in a noncentrosymmetric monoclinic structure (space group Pm) as the Cu-deficient counterpart but show a nearly stacking-fault-free phase, which is attributed to the emergence of an interstitial site. Consequently, the Cu-enriched samples show a pronounced enhancement of the second-harmonic generation (SHG) response compared to Cu-deficient compositions. Magnetically, the Cu-enriched crystals retain long-range antiferromagnetic order with a Neel temperature of TN ~ 33 K without a glassy state but manifest a distinct spin-flop transition along the polar b-axis that is absent in the Cu-deficient compositions. Furthermore, the electronic ground state evolves from insulating to doped semiconducting behavior upon Cu enrichment. Together, these results establish this material system as a unique and versatile platform for elucidating the interplay among composition, crystal defects, and multifunctional properties, offering a route to design magnetic polar systems with tunable quantum functionalities.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that increasing copper content in Cu–Mn–Si–Te crystals substantially reduces stacking faults and strengthens second-harmonic generation. The modified material retains antiferromagnetism while gaining tunable spin and electronic behavior, highlighting its potential for multifunctional semiconductor research.

articles.title_original: Anisotropic quantum transport and strain engineering in sub-5-nm gate-length HGeSiOH gersiloxene field-effect transistors
articles.title_en: Strain-Engineered HGeSiOH Gernsiloxene Transistors Show High Drive at Sub-5-nm Gate Lengths
articles.excerpt_original: 硅锗合金是成熟硅基微电子技术中的重要沟道材料，而二维半导体的原子级厚度为继续抑制短沟道效应提供了新的尺度优势。本文以实验已合成的H/OH终止二维Ge-Si合金H1-yGe1-xSix(OH)y锗硅氧烯（gersiloxene）为沟道，采用密度泛函理论结合非平衡格林函数的第一性原理量子输运方法，系统研究1-5 nm双栅场效应晶体管的尺度效应、输运各向异性及应变响应。PBE计算表明，HGeSiOH为带隙约1.50 eV的直接带隙半导体；其电子有效质量在面内不同方向均约为0.12m0，而空穴有效质量约为0.09-0.59m0，表现出显著的载流子依赖各向异性。对于5 nm栅长的器件，n型和p型开态电流最高分别达到1683和1528 µA/µm，且最佳输运取向的n/p型开态电流比约为1.10，体现出较好的互补驱动匹配。随着栅长由5 nm缩短至1 nm，单侧underlap长度相应由2 nm增加至6 nm的器件配置中，开态电流和跨导下降，亚阈值摆幅增大。这些变化反映了栅长与underlap共同变化对载流子输运及静电控制的综合影响。进一步分别沿各输运方向施加单轴压缩应变后，空穴有效质量的方向差异显著减小；在-4%应变下，四个代表性方向p型器件的开态电流集中在1624-1747 µA/µm，并全部超过国际半导体技术路线图高性能逻辑器件的参考值。结果表明，HGeSiOH兼具SiGe材料体系、二维沟道静电尺度优势和显著的应变可调性，是一种具有实验基础和高驱动能力的超短沟道Ge-Si基逻辑沟道材料
articles.summary_en: First-principles quantum-transport simulations indicate that HGeSiOH gersiloxene, an experimentally synthesized two-dimensional Ge–Si alloy, can support high-current complementary field-effect transistors with gate lengths of 1–5 nm. Compressive strain reduces hole-mass anisotropy and raises p-type on-state current above high-performance logic reference values in the modeled devices.

articles.title_original: Tunable scattering characteristics of a graphene-coated chiral spherical object
articles.title_en: Graphene-Coated Chiral Spheres Offer Tunable Electromagnetic Scattering
articles.excerpt_original: A tunable scattering analysis of a graphene-coated chiral spherical object has been presented using numerical evaluations. The standard Mie theory, along with the application of the impedance boundary condition, has been used to find the electromagnetic fields inside and outside the spherical object. Analytic expressions of the scattering coefficients for a graphene-coated chiral sphere have also been derived. It is investigated that by varying the chemical potential of the graphene coating, the overall scattering characteristics can be made tunable while keeping all other electromagnetic and geometrical parameters fixed. It is shown that an increase in the damping constant of a graphene layer dampens out the resonant peaks of the scattering efficiency of a graphene-coated chiral sphere. Likewise, it is found that the cloaking condition of a graphene-coated dielectric sphere can be suppressed by using a chiral sphere whose chirality is close to unity or greater than unity. Later on, we extend the proposed theory to the realistic chiral sphere that can be realized artificially.
articles.summary_en: Researchers present numerical and analytical models showing that graphene-coated chiral spheres can tune scattering behavior by adjusting graphene’s chemical potential. Increased damping suppresses resonances, while sphere chirality can inhibit cloaking in graphene-coated dielectric spheres.

articles.title_original: MXene-content-dependent phase evolution and electrochemical behavior of TiNb2O7/MXene composite anodes for lithium-ion batteries
articles.title_en: MXene Content Controls TiNb₂O₇ Anode Phase Evolution
articles.summary_en: Researchers investigate how MXene content affects phase evolution and electrochemical behavior in TiNb₂O₇/MXene composite anodes for lithium-ion batteries. The work is relevant to optimizing composite electrode design for energy-storage applications.

articles.title_original: Assembly of Graphene on SAMs and their performance to ORR.
articles.title_en: Graphene–SAM–Gold Electrodes Demonstrate Four-Electron Oxygen Reduction
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Here we present a new class of molecularly assembled electrode systems, composed of chemically reduced oxidized graphene (CRGO). The hydrophobic immobilization between this graphitic nanostructure on terminal groups (CH3) of molecular spacers was carried out using monolayers of self-assembled molecules (SAMs) of 4-Methylbenzenethiol (4-MBT), obtaining thus the [Au/4-MBT/CRGO] electrode system. On the other hand, the electrochemical characterization that is carried out through cyclic voltammetry and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) shows how the presence of CRGO reestablishes the electronic transfer and reduces the charge transfer resistance between the redox probe [Fe (CN)6]3-/4- and the electrode surface. Besides, the conductive images of AFM (AFM-c) reveal that the areas of greatest conductance are presented by CRGO nanostructures, immobilized on the graft of SAMs molecules in Au (111). Likewise, the characterization through Raman Spectroscopy indicated the presence of structural imperfections of this crystal lattice of carbon atoms, and a high number of localized defects on the surface of CRGO, due to the interaction that the CRGO nanostructure presents, when the assembly is established with the graft of SAMs in Au. The catalytic activity of this electrode system was examined for the reduction of O2 in aqueous media of NaOH and compared with that of Au (111) bare and Au (111) coated directly with Fe-phthalocyanine (FePc) molecules. The electrocatalytic studies carried out with [Au (111)/FePc] and [Au/4-MBT/CROG/FePc] electrodes show that the O2 reduction takes place by transferring 4-electron to give water. In this paper, the characterization and application of a CRGO modified gold electrode, a novel electrode system, are proposed.
articles.summary_en: Researchers assembled chemically reduced oxidized graphene on a gold electrode using 4-methylbenzenethiol self-assembled monolayers. The modified electrode restored electronic transfer, lowered charge-transfer resistance, and supported four-electron oxygen reduction to water in alkaline media.

articles.title_original: Crystals caught doping: Metallic Wigner crystals in rhombohedral graphene
articles.title_en: Theory predicts metallic Wigner crystals in rhombohedral graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Nearly a century after Wigner's initial proposal, electron crystals are now a topic of intense experimental and theoretical interest. However, most proposed crystalline phases are commensurate and therefore become insulating in the presence of even weak pinning. In this work we discuss when a commensurate Wigner crystal will spontaneously self dope and develop itinerant carriers, giving rise to an incommensurate and thus metallic Wigner crystal (MWC). We develop a general criterion for the instability of the commensurate crystal which involves the competition between the charge gap at commensurability and a ``packing bias'' whose sign selects whether electron or hole doping is preferred. We then apply these insights to rhombohedral multilayer graphene, where calculations for commensurate crystals reveal instabilities towards self-doping. Carrying out self-consistent Hartree-Fock over the landscape of incommensurate crystals reveals the phase diagram, where a broad MWC phase appears directly adjacent to an insulating Wigner crystal phase. Recent observations of an island of reversed Hall conductance near a putative Wigner crystal phase in rhombohedral graphene are naturally explained by our theory.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a criterion for when commensurate Wigner crystals self-dope and become metallic. Applying the model to rhombohedral multilayer graphene, they identified a broad metallic Wigner crystal phase and linked it to observed reversed Hall conductance.

articles.title_original: Synergistic integration of graphene-CNT-doped stearic acid PCM and graphene–metal oxide hybrid nanofluids for enhanced photovoltaic thermal–electrical performance
articles.title_en: Graphene–CNT PCM and Hybrid Nanofluids Improve PV Cooling
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract To enhance the durability of the solar PV systems, it is necessary to use novel materials and methods for cooling and disposal of unwanted heat. In this perspective, phase change materials (PCMs) with hybrid nanofluids are one of the best choices for efficient thermal management. This experiment proposes a novel PV cooling system that uses graphene and CNT nanoparticles (1:1) and (6 w/w%) added stearic acid as a PCM with hybrid nanofluids to maximize heat dissipation and system overall efficiency. The novelty lies in the synergistic combination of graphene-CNT-doped PCM (melting point 59 °C) with graphene-metal oxide hybrid nanofluids. Three hybrid nanofluids were prepared: G-TiO₂, G-Al₂O₃, and G-SiO₂, at a volume concentration of 0.5%, and different flow rates of 2, 4, 6, and 8 LPM were tested. The results proved that the 6 LPM flow rate, with the G-Al₂O₃ nanofluid, gave the best thermal and electrical results. In that, the enhanced absolute electrical efficiency was 4.5%, thermal efficiency by 8.3%, and the Nusselt number was 295 in comparison with the base fluid (DI water). Although the pressure drop and friction factor increased by 0.3 N/m² and 0.08, respectively, with G-SiO₂, it is still controllable with normal pumping. The proposed solar PV cooling system is highly applicable in building-integrated systems, hot climates, and hybrid renewable micro-grid systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers combined graphene–CNT-doped stearic acid phase-change material with graphene–metal oxide nanofluids for photovoltaic thermal management. At 6 LPM, the graphene–Al₂O₃ formulation delivered reported gains of 4.5% in electrical efficiency and 8.3% in thermal efficiency versus deionized water.

articles.title_original: Localization of hexagonal boron nitride color centers using patterned dielectric layers on graphene
articles.title_en: Patterned dielectrics localize hBN color centers on graphene
articles.excerpt_original: One of the most promising building blocks for the development of spin qubits, single-photon sources, and quantum sensors at room temperature, as well as 2D ultraviolet light-emitting diodes, is defect color centers in 2D hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). However, a significant requirement for the realization of such devices toward scalable technologies is the deterministic localization of hBN color centers. Here, we demonstrate a novel approach to the localization of hBN color center emission by using patterned dielectric layers grown on graphene via atomic layer deposition (ALD). While color center emission is quenched within areas where hBN is transferred directly on graphene due to charge transfer, it is maintained where hBN is transferred on micrometer-sized Al2O3 pillars, which act as barriers to charge transfer. Importantly, our approach allows for device architectures where graphene layers are used as top and bottom electrodes for the application of vertical electric fields, such as for carrier injection in electroluminescent devices, Stark shifting of color center emission, and charge state control of defect color centers. Furthermore, the use of ALD to grow dielectric layers directly on graphene allows for the control of tunnel barrier thicknesses with atomic layer precision, which is crucial for many of these device applications. Our work represents an important step toward the realization of a wide range of scalable device applications based on the deterministic localization of electrically controlled hBN color centers.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated deterministic localization of hexagonal boron nitride color-center emission using micrometer-scale Al2O3 pillars grown on graphene by atomic layer deposition. The approach preserves emission while enabling graphene electrodes, atomic-scale tunnel-barrier control, and electrically controlled quantum and optoelectronic devices.

articles.title_original: Graphene Oxide Aerogels with Ultra-Low Thermal Conductivity
articles.title_en: Reduced Graphene Oxide Aerogels Achieve Ultra-Low Thermal Conductivity
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Graphene oxide (GO)-based hydrogels and reduced graphene oxide (rGO)-based aerogels were synthesized and their thermal transport properties were characterized using steady-state and infrared thermography methodologies. GO was produced via a modified Hummers’ method and characterized by X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis. Self-assembled GO hydrogels exhibited thermal conductivity equal to 1.50 W/m·K, attributed to the formation of continuous thermally conductive networks at relatively high GO concentrations. In contrast, ultralight rGO aerogels with porosity approaching 99% demonstrated thermal conductivity of 0.021 W/m·K, which is 26% less than currently reported values for similar systems. The observed effect was attributed to extensive phonon scattering and suppressed solid and gaseous heat transport. The results highlight the strong dependence of thermal behavior on the microstructure and porosity of graphene-derived gels and demonstrate their potential for thermal management and insulation applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers synthesized graphene oxide hydrogels and reduced graphene oxide aerogels, measuring thermal conductivities of 1.50 W/m·K and 0.021 W/m·K, respectively. The findings link the aerogels’ performance to high porosity, phonon scattering, and suppressed heat transport, indicating potential for thermal insulation and management.

articles.title_original: Tunneling characteristics of twisted double bilayer graphene heterostructures
articles.title_en: Twisted bilayer graphene shows tunable resonant tunneling and negative differential resistance
articles.excerpt_original: Electron tunneling between sheets of bilayer Bernal graphene twisted at different small angles was studied experimentally and theoretically. The current–voltage characteristics exhibit resonant peaks, steps, and regions of negative differential resistance, the origin of which is explained by the intersections of energy- and momentum-shifted electron dispersions of adjacent layers. A theoretical analysis of tunneling transport demonstrated that the key to understanding this phenomenon lies in the competition between two contributions: between like (conduction–conduction or valence–valence) and unlike (conduction–valence) bands of parallel bilayer graphene sheets. A systematic evolution of the tunneling current patterns with increase in the twist angle is investigated. Polarization of electron wave function across graphene sublayers caused by displacement field within bilayer graphene is shown to strongly affect the tunneling probability, thus enhancing negative differential resistance due to Van Hove singularities at the band edges.
articles.summary_en: Experimental and theoretical work shows that twisted double bilayer graphene exhibits resonant peaks, step-like current–voltage behavior, and negative differential resistance. The findings link tunneling probabilities to band intersections, twist angle, displacement-field polarization, and Van Hove singularities, informing graphene-based electronic and tunneling devices.

articles.title_original: Analysis of Optothermal and Electronic Driving of Graphene Nanomechanical Resonators
articles.title_en: Electronic Driving Offers More Stable Performance in Graphene NEMS Resonators
articles.excerpt_original: Suspended graphene nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS) hold promise for sensing, signal processing, and quantum technologies, but actuation methods can introduce artifacts and limit performance. We present a systematic comparison of optical and electronic driving of suspended graphene resonators across multiple devices using full and fractional factorial designs. We assess how drive and probe laser positions, actuation method, resonator size, and drive order affect access to higher-order modes and frequency stability. Using scanning interferometric microscopy and amplitude spectra, we extract modal shapes and track resonant frequency behavior over time. Optical driving provides better access to higher-order modes but causes significantly greater frequency drift than electronic driving. Amplitude and mode visibility are highly sensitive to laser positioning, and drift behavior depends on resonator size, method, and test order. Time-resolved analysis shows non-monotonic frequency drift that persists across hours to weeks, consistent with permanent changes from laser-induced damage or contaminant ablation. We also observe apparent anti-resonance behavior tied to nodal shifts at the probe position. These results clarify the trade-offs between optical and electronic actuation and establish electronic driving as the more stable option for frequency-critical applications, while providing design guidance for improving NEMS performance and reliability.
articles.summary_en: A systematic study compares optical and electronic actuation of suspended graphene nanomechanical resonators, finding that optical driving accesses higher-order modes but causes greater frequency drift. Electronic driving is more stable for frequency-critical sensing and signal-processing applications, while laser positioning and induced damage remain important design considerations.

articles.title_original: Tunable Anisotropic Heat Transport in Structurally and Chemically Modified 3D Graphene
articles.title_en: Modified 3D Graphene Enables Tunable Anisotropic Heat Transport
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Three-dimensional graphene (3DG) networks offer a route to translate the high intrinsic thermal conductivity of graphene into macroscopic, freestanding architectures. However, heat transport in 3DG is not governed by the intrinsic conductivity of graphene alone, but by a hierarchy of pores, sheet orientation, network connectivity, and graphene-graphene junctions. Here, room-temperature cross-plane and in-plane thermal transport in pristine, compressed, welded, and doped 3DG structures is reported. Cross-plane thermal conductivity is measured using a differential 3ω method with transferable polyimide-supported metal heater lines, while in-plane thermal conductivity is obtained using a suspended four-probe electrothermal method. Mechanical compression strongly modifies the directional thermal response: cross-plane thermal conductivity decreases with densification, while in-plane transport remains comparatively enhanced, indicating that compression redistributes the graphene network into a more anisotropic, aligned architecture. Welding introduces an additional discrete thermal resistance, with increasing weld-plane numbers. Chemical modification suppresses both directions without producing the strong anisotropy amplification caused by rolling, suggesting that cross-plane heat flow remains dominated by phonon-mediated networks and junction resistance rather than electronic heat conduction. These results establish structural compression and weld-plane insertion as practical routes for programming anisotropic heat flow in freestanding 3DG.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that compression, welding, and chemical modification can program directional thermal conductivity in freestanding 3D graphene networks. The findings identify network alignment and junction resistance as key controls for thermal-management architectures.

articles.title_original: Nanoscale chemical engineering of Ti3C2Tx MXene multilayers through in situ electron beam irradiation in a TEM
articles.title_en: Electron-Beam Engineering Creates Patterned MXene Heterostructures
articles.excerpt_original: Defect engineering in low-dimensional materials is a powerful approach to tailor their structure and chemistry at the atomic scale, with high relevance for tuning physical properties. Here, we apply this strategy to MXenes, one of the largest families of two-dimensional (2D) materials, and demonstrate the use of a highly focused scanning transmission electron microscope (STEM) beam for the structural and chemical nanoengineering of titanium carbide (Ti3C2Tx) multilayers. By adjusting the beam energy, electron dose, and scanning parameters, Ti3C2Tx multilayers were irradiated at 80 and 300 keV and characterized in situ using annular dark-field imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS). The irradiation induces gradual structural and chemical modifications, largely driven by the selective sputtering of atomic species and MXene layers. We identify irradiation conditions that selectively remove Cl or F surface terminations while largely preserving the Ti3C2 framework, whereas other conditions promote preferential carbon removal, in agreement with theoretical predictions. Most notably, electron irradiation drives the migration and accumulation of initially dilute nitrogen impurities within the irradiated regions, leading to the formation of nitrogen-rich titanium carbonitride (Ti3CyNzTx) nanodomains embedded in the Ti3C2Tx multilayers. These laterally patterned carbide/carbonitride architectures constitute in-plane MXene heterostructures with nanometer-scale spatial control. These results demonstrate that electron irradiation can be used to locally tailor MXene composition and create nanoscale architectures beyond those accessible through conventional chemical synthesis.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used in situ electron-beam irradiation to selectively modify surface terminations and carbon content in Ti3C2Tx MXene multilayers. The process also produced nitrogen-rich titanium carbonitride nanodomains, enabling nanoscale in-plane heterostructures without conventional chemical synthesis.

articles.title_original: Hydrogen-bond-cross-linked PVA/MXene films for durable triboelectric nanogenerators and gesture sensing
articles.title_en: Hydrogen-Bonded PVA/MXene Films Improve Durable Triboelectric Gesture Sensors
articles.excerpt_original: Flexible self-powered sensors based on transition metal carbides/nitrides (MXenes) are considered for intelligent human-machine interfaces (HMIs), but their use is limited by ambient oxidation and mechanical fragility during repetitive deformation. In this work, a surface-coating strategy is used to prepare PVA/MXene composite films, in which poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) is bonded to MXene through interfacial hydrogen bonds. The PVA layer reduces MXene’s exposure to moisture and oxygen and limits crack propagation under cyclic mechanical stress. The resulting triboelectric nanogenerator delivers a peak output voltage of 50 V with an Ecoflex counter layer and a maximum power density of 6 μW/cm<sup>2</sup>. The device charges a 2.2 μF commercial capacitor to ≈2.7 V within 60 s. A self-powered sensor array combined with a machine-learning model is used to distinguish six hand gestures; a support vector machine classifier reaches 93.33% ± 6.09% accuracy on the collected signals (45 samples, stratified 5-fold cross-validation). These results support the development of durable flexible self-powered devices and HMIs.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed PVA/MXene composite films that reduce oxidation and crack propagation during repeated deformation. The triboelectric nanogenerator produced 50 V and enabled machine-learning-based recognition of six hand gestures with 93.33% ± 6.09% accuracy.

The dataset contains 15 structures: monolayer and AA-stacked bilayer Nb2CS2, Nb2CSe2, Ta2CS2 and Ta2CSe2, and commensurate 2x2 M2CS2 / 1x1 CrBr3 heterostructures (Ta2CS2 monolayer and bilayer, Nb2CS2 monolayer and bilayer) with CrBr3 below (CrBr3-bottom) or above (CrBr3-top) the MXene. articles.title_original: Dual-anchored interfacial and sheet-sphere hybrid network engineering for thermally conductive, mechanically robust EVA/BN photovoltaic encapsulants
articles.title_en: Hybrid Boron Nitride EVA Encapsulant Improves PV Thermal Management
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Encapsulation films combining high thermal conductivity, stable electrical insulation, and excellent mechanical properties are urgently needed for photovoltaic modules. However, achieving all these properties simultaneously in conventional ethylene–vinyl acetate copolymer (EVA) encapsulants remains a significant challenge. Herein, a synergistic three-tier strategy integrating EVA matrix crosslinking, a sheet-sphere hybrid filler network, and dual-anchored interfacial engineering is proposed to resolve this conflict. Specifically, 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (KH550) is grafted onto both the EVA matrix and the boron nitride (BN) filler surfaces via radical coupling and hydroxylation, respectively, establishing a dual-anchored interface of covalent bonds and hydrogen bonds. Combined with a sheet-sphere hybrid BN architecture (f-BN) constructed from hexagonal boron nitride microplatelets and spherical boron nitride microspheres, and a crosslinked EVA matrix (cEVA), this design enables the as-prepared cEVA/f-BN composite encapsulation film to achieve a high through-plane thermal conductivity‌ of 2.96 W·m⁻ 1 ·K⁻ 1 , representing a 1245% enhancement compared to the pure EVA film. Remarkably, the composite maintains a tensile strength of 8.99 MPa, an elongation of 89.75% at a filler loading of 110 phr, and a volume resistivity exceeding 10 14 Ω·cm. The composite film also exhibits high solar reflectance (91.09%) and infrared emissivity (96.17%), which in synergy with its enhanced thermal conductivity, reduce the photovoltaic module temperature by 5.34 ℃.This study not only demonstrates a good combination of thermal and mechanical properties in EVA encapsulants but also provides a broadly applicable interfacial design reference for the development of polymer composite
articles.summary_en: Researchers engineered a crosslinked EVA encapsulant with dual-anchored interfaces and a hybrid boron nitride filler network. The film reached 2.96 W/m·K through-plane thermal conductivity while retaining electrical insulation and mechanical flexibility, reducing photovoltaic module temperature by 5.34°C.

articles.title_original: On the origin of nonreciprocal charge transport in topological insulator BiSbTeSe2
articles.title_en: Gate-tunable nonreciprocal transport demonstrated in BiSbTeSe2 topological-insulator devices
articles.excerpt_original: Nonreciprocal charge transport provides an effective approach for probing direction-dependent charge dynamics and spin-momentum-locked electronic states. Here, we report highly gate-tunable nonreciprocal charge transport in a dual-gated BiSbTeSe2 topological insulator device. The second-harmonic longitudinal resistance is linear in both current and magnetic field. The nonreciprocal response reaches its maximum near the charge neutrality point, exhibits sign reversals on either side, and is strongly suppressed once the Fermi level enters the bulk states. We suggest that the nonreciprocal response is attributed to the inhomogeneity of spin-momentum locking in the topological surface states. The nonreciprocal signal near the charge neutrality point is about one order of magnitude larger than that without gate modulation and remains robust up to 300 K, highlighting BiSbTeSe2 as a promising platform for room-temperature nonlinear electronics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report strongly gate-tunable nonreciprocal charge transport in dual-gated BiSbTeSe2, with a response enhanced near charge neutrality and suppressed in bulk states. The signal remains robust to 300 K, indicating potential for room-temperature nonlinear electronics based on topological surface states.

articles.title_original: Schottky-interface-controlled mode-reconfigurable photoresponse in all-2D MESFET
articles.title_en: All-2D MESFET Enables Low-Voltage Dual-Mode Photosensing
articles.excerpt_original: Mode-reconfigurable optoelectronic devices integrating fast photodetection and photosynaptic response are promising for adaptive visual sensing and neuromorphic preprocessing. However, most reported dual-mode devices still rely on global metal–oxide–semiconductor gating and uncontrolled dielectric-interface trapping, which limit local interfacial control and often require relatively high operating voltages. Here, we demonstrate a VSe2-gated WS2 van der Waals (vdW) metal–semiconductor field-effect transistor (MESFET) with Schottky-interface-controlled dual-mode photoresponse. The VSe2/WS2 Schottky contact induces strong depletion, enabling enhancement-mode-like operation at low gate voltage. By tuning the depletion region and interfacial photogating, the device switches from fast photodetection to persistent photosynaptic response. Under 520 nm illumination, the photodetection mode shows rise/fall times of 4.9/6.77 ms and a responsivity of 395 mA W−1. In the photosynaptic mode, the device exhibits excitatory postsynaptic current, paired-pulse facilitation, and a transition from short-term to long-term plasticity. The persistent response further enables temporal filtering for neuromorphic vision preprocessing. This work provides a strategy for low-voltage dual-mode optoelectronic devices based on vdW MESFETs.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated a VSe2-gated WS2 van der Waals MESFET that switches between fast photodetection and persistent photosynaptic response through Schottky-interface-controlled depletion and photogating. The device achieved 395 mA W−1 responsivity with millisecond response times and supported temporal filtering for neuromorphic vision preprocessing.

articles.title_original: Controlling carrier localization in 2D lead-free halide perovskites for dual-functional photodetector and photosynapse
articles.title_en: Solvent Engineering Enables Dual-Mode Tin Perovskite Phototransistors
articles.excerpt_original: Low-dimensional tin halide perovskites are regarded as ideal channel materials for phototransistors owing to their high carrier mobility and light absorption coefficient. To date, phototransistors have been developed along two distinct directions: photodetectors with rapid response and recovery dynamics, and photosynapses with persistent photoconductivity and slow decay characteristics for emulating long-term memory. However, strategies to simultaneously achieve these divergent functionalities remain poorly understood. In this work, the defect density and carrier dynamics in PEA2SnI4 films are tuned through a solvent engineering approach, enabling dual operational modes for photodetector and photosynapse devices. Phototransistors based on dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) exhibit defect-assisted carrier localization, leading to robust synaptic behavior. In comparison, 1,3-dimethyl-2-imidazolidinone (DMI) suppresses trapping sites, enabling fast photoresponse for photodetection. This work provides insights into the defect-mediated photoresponse mechanisms and offers a rationale for tailoring tin perovskite phototransistors in multifunctional optoelectronics.
articles.summary_en: Researchers tuned carrier localization in lead-free tin halide perovskite films to switch between fast photodetection and persistent photosynaptic behavior. Solvent selection controlled defect-assisted trapping, offering a route to multifunctional optoelectronic devices.

articles.title_original: Modulating and stabilizing MoS2 electronics via a sulfur capping layer
articles.title_en: Sulfur capping stabilizes MoS2 transistor electronics
articles.excerpt_original: Two-dimensional semiconductors, featuring atomic-scale thickness, excellent electrostatic gate control, and outstanding electrical properties, hold great promise for next-generation electronics. Recently, monolayer MoS2, a typical two-dimensional semiconductor, has been extensively explored for field-effect transistors (FETs). However, its atomically thin channel is highly sensitive to environmental exposure and interfacial perturbations, leading to significant performance degradation. Here, we report a low-temperature (200 °C), intrinsic sulfur passivation strategy to form a nondestructive capping layer on monolayer MoS2 FETs. This capping layer effectively isolates the channel from ambient species while passivating sulfur vacancy defects. As a result, the electrical performance is markedly improved, leading to a positive threshold voltage shift of 1.5 V and a substantial reduction in hysteresis from 2 V to 160 mV. Notably, the devices exhibit excellent environmental stability, maintaining their performance after 180 days under ambient conditions. Based on this approach, rail-to-rail inverters are realized using a pristine MoS2 load transistor and an S-capped MoS2 driver transistor, achieving a high voltage gain of 175.11 with symmetric noise margins (noise margin high ≈ 1.82 V and noise margin low ≈ 1.82 V). Importantly, large-scale inverter arrays demonstrate excellent device uniformity and reproducibility in performance. Furthermore, the scalability of this strategy is demonstrated via various fundamental logic circuits, including NOR and NAND gates, as well as a five-stage ring oscillator. These results highlight the effectiveness of sulfur passivation in enabling high-performance, stable, and scalable MoS2-based electronic and integrated circuit applications.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report a low-temperature sulfur passivation layer that reduces hysteresis and improves environmental stability in monolayer MoS2 transistors. The approach enabled uniform inverter arrays and basic logic circuits, supporting scalable two-dimensional semiconductor electronics.

articles.title_original: Optical signature of bias-induced carrier injection in a WSe2/MoS2 heterostructure diode
articles.title_en: Bias-Driven Carrier Injection Revealed in WSe2/MoS2 Diode
articles.excerpt_original: We investigate the bias-dependent photoluminescence (PL) response of a WSe2/MoS2 heterostructure diode. Under forward bias, trion-related emission in WSe2 is markedly enhanced, whereas reverse bias produces minimal spectral changes. This asymmetric response cannot be explained by electric-field effects alone and instead reflects carrier injection at the functional interface. These results demonstrate that PL provides a direct optical probe of carrier injection in an operating van der Waals heterostructure. More broadly, this approach establishes spatially resolved PL spectroscopy as a versatile tool for pinpointing the interfaces governing device operation in van der Waals heterostructures.
articles.summary_en: Researchers show that forward-bias photoluminescence enhancement in a WSe2/MoS2 heterostructure diode directly indicates carrier injection at the interface. Spatially resolved photoluminescence could help diagnose operating interfaces in van der Waals semiconductor devices.

articles.title_original: Electronic properties and topological aspects of graphene nanohelicoids
articles.title_en: Graphene nanohelicoids show tunable electronic and topological states
articles.excerpt_original: We introduce graphene nanohelicoids, geometric analogs of graphene nanoribbons, in which the honeycomb lattice is embedded on a helicoidal surface. Starting from the three-dimensional helical structure, we construct effective one-dimensional lattice models with band structures characterized by a momentum-shifted particle-hole relation E v ( k ) = − E c ( k + π ) that reflects an antichiral symmetry arising from the nonsymmorphic symmetry. A systematic investigation of graphene nanohelicoids using the tight-binding approximation reveals a number of trends upon varying width and edge orientation, for instance, alternating transitions between semiconducting and metallic regimes. As the structure width varies, the band gap periodically closes and reopens, accompanied by an alternating Zak phase that switches between trivial and nontrivial. Using an analytic tight-binding model with a continuous deformation of the graphene nanohelicoids, we explain the origin of width- and termination-dependent band inversion and alternating Zak phase, and derive the relationship between the termination-resolved index and the sublattice symmetry operator in one-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems.
articles.summary_en: Researchers introduce graphene nanohelicoids, helicoidal counterparts to graphene nanoribbons, and model their electronic structure using tight-binding methods. Varying width and edge termination drives alternating metallic or semiconducting behavior, band-gap closing and reopening, and switches between trivial and nontrivial Zak phases.

articles.title_original: Lattice thermal conductivity of Ti3C2 MXene via deep-learning potential
articles.title_en: Deep-learning study models lattice thermal conductivity in Ti3C2 MXene
articles.summary_en: Academic research uses a deep-learning potential to investigate lattice thermal conductivity in Ti3C2 MXene. The work may support computational screening and thermal-management design for MXene-based materials.

articles.title_original: Single Photon Emitters in Monolayer Semiconductors Coupled to Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Nanoantennas on Silica and Gold Substrates
articles.title_en: TMD Nanoantennas Enhance Single-Photon Emitters on Silica and Gold
articles.excerpt_original: ABSTRACT Single photon emitters (SPEs) in transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) monolayers are attractive for quantum information applications. Strain in the monolayer, induced by underlying Mie resonators, localizes SPEs to positions co‐located with photonic hotspots, providing control over their optical properties. However, resonators made from traditional materials such as silicon or gallium phosphide (GaP), often require a high refractive index substrate resulting in light losses and limited photonic enhancement. Here, we use nanoantennas (NAs) fabricated from a multilayer TMD WS 2 , allowing complete flexibility with the choice of substrate due to the adhesive van der Waals forces, enabling high refractive index contrast or the use of highly reflective metallic surfaces. We demonstrate formation of SPEs in WSe 2 monolayers transferred onto WS 2 NAs on both SiO 2 and Au substrates, enabling strong photonic enhancements and increased single photon collection. We find enhancement of quantum efficiencies (QE) averaging to 43% (7%) for SPEs on WS 2 NAs on a SiO 2 (Au) substrate. We further combine the advantages offered by both dielectric and metallic substrates to numerically simulate an optimized NA geometry for maximum WSe 2 single photon excitation, emission and collection yielding fluorescence enhancements of over 4 (5) orders of magnitude compared to vacuum (flat SiO 2 /Si surface).
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrated enhanced single-photon emission from WSe₂ monolayers coupled to WS₂ nanoantennas on both silica and gold substrates. The platform achieved average quantum efficiencies of 43% on silica and 7% on gold, with simulations predicting fluorescence enhancements exceeding four orders of magnitude.

articles.title_original: One-Dimensional Structural Boundaries in 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides: Physics, Engineering, and Functional Electronics
articles.title_en: Review Maps One-Dimensional Boundaries in 2D Materials for Electronics
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) materials, including graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), provide atomically thin platforms for next-generation electronic, optoelectronic, and van der Waals (vdW) heterostructure devices. For each class, we discuss the relationships among formation mechanisms, atomic structures, electronic properties, deterministic synthesis strategies, and emerging device concepts. By comparing these boundaries in TMD monolayers and in moiré and sliding-ferroelectric TMD bilayers, with bilayer graphene as a reference system for stacking domain walls, we show that their electronic functionalities are governed by distinct physical mechanisms, including atomic stitching, defect-core motifs, symmetry-defined metallicity, stacking topology, strain relaxation, and local electrostatic reconstruction.
