articles.summary_en: A topical review examines grain boundaries, mirror twin boundaries, and domain walls in transition metal dichalcogenides, using bilayer graphene as a reference for stacking domain walls. It links boundary structure and formation mechanisms to electronic properties, deterministic synthesis, and emerging device concepts.

articles.title_original: Graphene Josephson diodes from asymmetric disorder
articles.title_en: Graphene Josephson diodes achieve over 20% supercurrent rectification
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Josephson diodes are non-reciprocal superconducting devices characterized by different switching currents depending on the current flow direction. They recently attracted considerable theoretical and experimental attention, in view of their possible application as rectifying elements in the field of superconducting electronics, and as probes to investigate symmetry breaking mechanisms in mesoscopic systems. In this work, we show that graphene Josephson junctions provide rectification of supercurrent with an efficiency exceeding 20%. The effect appears applying a mT out-of-plane magnetic field and is enhanced close to the nodes of the Fraunhofer interference pattern. Our findings are consistent with a theoretical model that considers long-range scattering potentials in the junction as the symmetry-breaking mechanism, which yields supercurrent rectification in highly transparent junctions. While graphene stands out as an ultra-clean transmission medium, our work shows that unavoidable residual disorder is sufficient to promote this effect.
articles.summary_en: Researchers report that graphene Josephson junctions can rectify supercurrent with efficiency exceeding 20% under a millitesla-scale out-of-plane magnetic field. The study attributes the effect to residual long-range disorder and highlights potential use in superconducting electronics and symmetry-breaking studies.

articles.title_original: Graphene-Enabled Microstructured PDMS Triboelectric Nanogenerator for Self-Powered Human-Machine Interfaces
articles.title_en: Graphene–PDMS Triboelectric Generator Enables Self-Powered Gesture Sensing
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) provide a promising route toward self-powered wearable sensors by converting low-frequency human motion into electrical signals. However, the practical use of soft polymer TENGs in human-machine interfaces remains limited by inefficient contact formation, low charge density, and restricted power delivery. Here, a graphene-enabled microstructured PDMS TENG is developed for self-powered gesture sensing. The device combines two complementary design strategies. Micropatterning the PDMS surface improves interfacial contact, pressure localisation and contact-separation recovery, while graphene incorporation introduces 2D polymer-filler interfaces that enhance dielectric polarisation, interfacial charge storage and charge induction within the elastomeric matrix. The optimised graphene@PDMS tribolayer delivers an open-circuit voltage of 150 V, transferred charge of 34 nC, and a power density of 1.92 W m⁻², showing a 16-fold improvement over pristine microstructured PDMS. The enhanced output is attributed to an effective pre-percolation graphene network that strengthens interfacial polarisation while avoiding dominant leakage and electrostatic screening. Integrated into a five-channel wearable glove, the TENG array generates finger-specific voltage patterns for proof-of-concept self-powered sign-language recognition. This work establishes a simple 2D-material-enabled microstructure-composite engineering strategy for high-output flexible TENGs and wearable human-machine interfaces.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a microstructured graphene–PDMS triboelectric nanogenerator delivering 150 V, 34 nC transferred charge, and 1.92 W m⁻² power density—16 times the output of pristine microstructured PDMS. Integrated into a five-channel glove, the device demonstrated finger-specific sign-language recognition for wearable human–machine interfaces.

articles.title_original: Scanning gate microscopy modulation of supercurrent in graphene Josephson junctions
articles.title_en: Scanning-gate microscopy maps supercurrent in graphene Josephson junctions
articles.excerpt_original: Graphene Josephson junctions (JJs) represent an excellent platform for quantum technologies, thanks to the combination of high carrier mobility, ballistic transport, and gate-tunable critical currents, preserved even under quantizing magnetic fields. Investigating the spatial distribution of supercurrent flow could be crucial for elucidating transport mechanisms and advancing the engineering of these devices. In this work, we employ a scanning gate microscope to investigate supercurrent transport in hexagonal boron nitride-encapsulated graphene JJs. We study the supercurrent modulation as a function of tip voltage bias and tip-to-sample distance and provide a complete characterization of the tip-induced modulation. Our experimental results are quantitatively consistent with numerical simulations and pave the way toward local mapping and manipulation of gate-tunable superconducting phenomena with unprecedented spatial resolution.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used scanning-gate microscopy to characterize tip-induced modulation of supercurrent in hexagonal-boron-nitride-encapsulated graphene Josephson junctions. The results agree with numerical simulations and support local mapping and manipulation of gate-tunable superconducting phenomena for quantum-device research.

articles.title_original: Cryogenic Graphene-Based Phase Modulators for Quantum Information Processing
articles.title_en: Cryogenic Graphene Phase Modulators Designed for Quantum Photonics
articles.excerpt_original: Electro-optic modulators are key components for photonic quantum computing, particularly in fully cryogenic integrated platforms where low loss and compactness are critical. We present a systematic theoretical investigation of compact dual-layer graphene (DSLG) electro-optic phase modulators integrated on silicon nitride (Si 3 N 4 ) waveguides, with an emphasis on cryogenic operation. By combining electromagnetic simulations with a physically consistent description of graphene conductivity based on the Kubo formalism, we analyze the interplay between electrostatic tuning, optical mode confinement, and material-dependent losses. We show that cryogenic operation enhances device performance by sharpening the Fermi–Dirac distribution, enabling access to the Pauli-blocking regime at lower Fermi levels and reducing the required modulation length. Through optimization of the waveguide geometry, dielectric spacer thickness and permittivity, and graphene quality, we identify regimes that simultaneously minimize insertion loss and device footprint under realistic voltage constraints. The optimized designs achieve near-pure phase modulation with insertion losses below 0.3 dB for modulation lengths below 50 µm at 10 K, while maintaining GHz-scale bandwidths. These results provide quantitative design guidelines for low-loss, compact, cryogenic graphene phase modulators for scalable integrated quantum photonics.
articles.summary_en: A theoretical study models dual-layer graphene phase modulators integrated with silicon nitride waveguides for cryogenic quantum information systems. Simulations indicate insertion losses below 0.3 dB, modulation lengths under 50 µm, and GHz-scale bandwidth at 10 K, subject to modeled material and device assumptions.

articles.title_original: DFT structures: Cu coordination on graphene oxide (supporting data for "Breaking the permeability bottleneck of graphene oxide membranes through pre-assembly nanosheet crumpling")
articles.title_en: DFT Structures Detail Copper Coordination in Graphene Oxide Membranes
articles.excerpt_original: Relaxed atomic structures from the density functional theory (DFT) part of the manuscript "Breaking the permeability bottleneck of graphene oxide membranes through pre-assembly nanosheet crumpling" (main-text Fig. 4; Supplementary Figs. S8-S12 and Tables S1-S4). The archive contains 21 structures in VASP POSCAR format. Contents: the clean graphene oxide (GO) sheet (C72H4O8, 6x6 graphene supercell with epoxy and hydroxyl groups); a single Cu atom on the GO basal plane at the epoxy-Cu-OH ground state, the two-epoxy bridge, the epoxy-OH bridge and two bare-carbon top sites; Cu2, Cu3 and Cu4 clusters at the GO pocket; metal-free, Cu-bridged and Na-bridged GO bilayers; H2O and benzene isolated, on GO and on Cu-GO; and the isolated Cu atom, isolated Na atom and bulk fcc Cu references.
articles.summary_en: Open-access supporting data provides 21 VASP structures modeling copper atoms and clusters coordinated with graphene oxide, including Cu-bridged bilayers and interactions with water and benzene. The dataset supports research into improving graphene oxide membrane permeability through nanosheet crumpling and metal-mediated assembly.

articles.title_original: Two-Dimensional (2D) MXene-Based Nanocomposites for High-Performance Supercapacitors
articles.title_en: MXene–Graphene Nanocomposites for High-Performance Supercapacitors
articles.excerpt_original: The exhaustion of conventional energy sources such as fossil fuels, coupled with the growing energy needs, emphasizes the urgent need to develop alternative energy sources. The electrochemical energy storage (EES) systems have attracted tremendous interest in both the academic and industrial sectors. Among EES devices, supercapacitors have recently emerged as promising EES devices due to their remarkable power density, fast charge/discharge rate, and excellent cycling stability. The tendency to advance EES systems, including supercapacitors, to new frontiers is experiencing a strong push toward advanced material designs with improved electrochemical performance. While electrode materials play significant roles in governing the energy storage mechanism, electrode architecture is equally important. Recently, MXenes have emerged as multifaceted two-dimensional (2D) materials, which are surface-modified carbides or nitrides, providing their flexibility and variable compositions. This book chapter is focused on 2D MXene-based nanocomposites as emerging electrode materials with their electrochemical performance for supercapacitor applications. Moreover, we briefly discuss MXene’s structure along with their various properties and shed light on MXene nanocomposites with various families, including graphene, transition metal oxides (TMOs), metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), polymers, transition metal sulfides (TMSs), etc., together with their excellent electrochemical performance for supercapacitors. Finally, the central future outlooks and perspectives for MXene-based electrodes for supercapacitors are highlighted.
articles.summary_en: This academic book chapter reviews MXene-based nanocomposite electrodes for supercapacitors, including graphene, transition-metal oxides, polymers, and other materials. It examines how material composition and electrode architecture can improve electrochemical performance and outlines future research directions.

articles.title_original: MBenes beyond MXenes: the next frontier of 2D boride materials for multivalent ion energy storage devices
articles.title_en: MBenes Emerge as 2D Boride Candidates for Multivalent-Ion Storage
articles.summary_en: The research reviews MBenes—two-dimensional boride materials—as a potential platform for multivalent-ion energy-storage devices. It highlights their prospects beyond MXenes, although the source provides no specific performance or commercialization evidence.

articles.title_original: Energetics of hexagonal boron nitride nanoflakes adsorbed on hexagonal boron nitride sheet
articles.title_en: DFT study examines hBN nanoflake energetics and bilayer stacking
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The energetics of triangular hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) nanoflakes with clean edges are studied using density functional theory (DFT), with particular attention to their size and edge. Formation energies of triangular hBN nanoflakes depend on the flake size, edge termination, and chemical potentials of B and N atoms: The flakes prefer N termination when borazine (B₃N₃H₆) and ammonia borane (BNH₆) are their source molecules, whereas B termination is stabilized for diborane (B₂H₆) molecule. The energetics of the flakes on the hBN sheet are also investigated to provide theoretical insight into the nucleation processes of the hBN bilayer. The flakes are bistable at or around the angles of 0˚ and 60˚, corresponding to AA’ and AB stacking, respectively. The energy barriers for rotation increase with increasing flake size, indicating that the stacking orientation of the hBN bilayer is determined at the early stage of nucleation.
articles.summary_en: Researchers used density functional theory to analyze how hBN nanoflake size, edge termination, and precursor chemistry affect formation energies. The study finds that stacking orientation in hBN bilayers is established during early nucleation, with rotational barriers increasing as flakes grow.

articles.title_original: Nonlinear Optical Fingerprints of Defects in Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.title_en: Defect Signatures Enable Nonlinear Optical Probing of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) defects are promising building blocks for quantum photonics and sensing, yet their nonlinear optical signatures remain poorly understood. We use first-principles calculations to determine the polarization-resolved linear, second-order, and third-order susceptibilities of multilayer h-BN containing vacancies and carbon-based defect complexes. Defects weakly affect the linear response but strongly enhance nonlinear susceptibilities through symmetry breaking and resonant defect transitions. Carbon complexes produce orders-of-magnitude increases in second-harmonic generation and distinct polarization-dependent spectra that differentiate defects with identical composition but different geometry. Third-harmonic generation is also enhanced, although it is less sensitive to local structure. Measurements on carbon-doped h-BN qualitatively support these trends. These results establish nonlinear spectroscopy as a powerful probe of defect identity and geometry in h-BN and provide a route to defect-engineered nonlinear quantum photonics.
articles.summary_en: First-principles calculations show that vacancies and carbon-related defects strongly enhance nonlinear optical responses in multilayer hexagonal boron nitride, particularly second-harmonic generation. Polarization-dependent spectra can distinguish defects with identical compositions but different geometries, supporting applications in quantum photonics and sensing.

articles.title_original: Microstructural evolution, tribological and corrosion behavior of spark plasma sintering-processed Cu-h-BN-316L SS hybrid composites
articles.title_en: Spark-Plasma-Sintered Cu–h-BN–316L Steel Hybrid Composites Studied
articles.summary_en: Academic research examines the microstructural evolution, tribological performance, and corrosion behavior of hybrid composites combining copper, hexagonal boron nitride, and 316L stainless steel processed by spark plasma sintering. The work is relevant to composite-material durability and wear research, but the available information does not establish commercial application or performance advantages.

articles.title_original: Advances on jacutingaite ( Pt 2 HgSe 3 )-based materials: Natural mineral to tunable topological phases
articles.title_en: Jacutingaite Emerges as a Tunable Topological Quantum Material
articles.excerpt_original: Jacutingaite, Pt 2 HgSe 3 , has emerged as a model van der Waals material linking mineralogy, solid-state chemistry, and topological quantum physics. Single crystals of bulk Pt 2 HgSe 3 experimentally synthesized under high-pressure and high-resolution angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy reveal a gapped Dirac nodal-line structure along with the surface states with multiple saddle points and van Hove singularities. Furthermore, under hydrostatic pressure, transport measurements show a structure phase transition accompanied by superconductivity, with T c reaching approximately 4.4 K at 88.8 GPa. Density functional theory calculations predict bulk Pt 2 HgSe 3 to possess dual topology, characterized by weak Z 2 topology and mirror-symmetry-protected crystalline topology. Monolayer Pt 2 HgSe 3 was predicted to realize a Kane–Mele-type quantum spin Hall state with a spin-orbit induced gap of ∼ 0.15 – 0.5 eV , a result supported by early experimental signatures. Other theoretical studies predicted that the electronic structure and topological properties can be tuned by layer thickness, strain, electric fields, and pressures. Bilayers are shown to be initially trivial due to layer-internal inversion asymmetry, but with encapsulation within hexagonal boron nitride undergoes an electronically driven topological phase transition which narrows the trivial band gap, and a modest out-of-plane electric field reinverts the bands to restore their topology, though these mechanisms remain to be verified experimentally. articles.summary_en: A research update examines bulk, monolayer, and bilayer Pt₂HgSe₃, highlighting predicted quantum spin Hall states, pressure-induced superconductivity near 4.4 K, and tunability through strain, fields, doping, and heterostructures. Experimental validation remains incomplete for several proposed bilayer and engineering mechanisms.

articles.title_original: Fully Automated Wannier Disentanglement via Projectability Selection in Gaussian and Augmented Plane-Wave Frameworks
articles.title_en: Automated Wannier-Function Workflow Validated Across Diverse Materials
articles.excerpt_original: This record holds the calculation data of the paper "Fully Automated Wannier Disentanglement via Projectability Selection in Gaussian and Augmented Plane-Wave Frameworks" by W. P. Comaskey and J. L. Mendoza-Cortes. The paper derives an energy ceiling from the target number of Wannier functions and freezes every Bloch state below it. The projectability of each state onto a localized target basis is used to select the admitted states, to add missing conduction channels and to certify where the per-state classification disagrees with the energy ordering. The method is implemented in LCAO2Wannier 1.0.0 for CRYSTAL (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23484953) and in wien2wannier 3.0 for WIEN2k (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23485188), a modified version of wien2wannier by J. Kuneš et al., Comput. Phys. Commun. 181, 1888 (2010) (https://wien2wannier.github.io). The record holds the inputs, command lines and outputs needed to regenerate every overlap, projection and hand-off file and to check every reported number. Large files that can be regenerated, namely the Wannier90 .mmn, .amn and .chk files and the WIEN2k vector files, are not included. REPRODUCE_LCAO.md and REPRODUCE_LAPW.md give the regeneration steps and settings for each material and run, and NOT_ARCHIVED.md lists the results that cannot be regenerated from the record. The CRYSTAL part (CRYSTAL23 v1.0.1 and LCAO2Wannier) contains the original CRYSTAL input decks and the properties outputs (real-space Hamiltonian and overlap matrices and the basis) of bulk h-BN and MgB2 and of SnTe and the Bi bilayer with spin–orbit coupling, which are the input of LCAO2Wannier. Reruns of the decks that reproduce the printed total energies are included. For each run the record has the command line, the Wannier90 input and output record
articles.summary_en: Researchers released reproducible calculation data and software implementations for automating Wannier disentanglement using projectability selection. The workflow is demonstrated on h-BN, MgB2, SnTe and a Bi bilayer, supporting more efficient electronic-structure modeling rather than a specific commercial application.

articles.title_original: Nonlinear circular dichroism reveals the local Berry curvature
articles.title_en: Nonlinear circular dichroism measures local Berry curvature in monolayer WSe₂
articles.excerpt_original: The transfer of angular momentum between light and crystalline solids during nonlinear optical processes is typically interpreted in terms of angular momentum conservation and the rotational symmetry of the crystal lattice. However, these cornerstone principles rely on macroscopic symmetry arguments, providing little insight into the microscopic origin of angular momentum transfer. Here we show that changes in the spin angular momentum of light in high-harmonic generation processes, which we probe via nonlinear circular dichroism, are directly proportional to the local Berry curvature at a single optical resonance, therefore establishing a link between nonlinear light–matter interactions and the quantum geometry of electronic states. We demonstrate this relationship using second-harmonic generation in monolayer WSe2, using circularly polarized light to break time-reversal symmetry and lift the degeneracy between the valleys. The resulting second-harmonic circular dichroism can be controlled through the intensity and helicity of the circularly polarized light, hence offering a method for the control and readout of the optically probed Berry curvature.
articles.summary_en: Researchers demonstrate that nonlinear circular dichroism directly tracks local Berry curvature at an optical resonance. Using second-harmonic generation in monolayer WSe₂, the study shows that Berry curvature can be controlled and read through the intensity and helicity of circularly polarized light.

articles.title_original: Compound-specific memory demand determines when a research group and a computing centre benefit from sharing information in two-dimensional semiconductor screening
articles.title_en: Study Finds Limited Value in Sharing Memory Data for 2D Semiconductor Screening
articles.excerpt_original: Screening two-dimensional semiconductors with density functional theory (DFT), the standard electronic-structure method, involves two parties who know each other only qualitatively: a research group holding the candidate list and a computing centre that knows its nodes. Sharing information helps either party only if a calculation’s demand on the node depends on the compound. Thirty transition-metal dichalcogenide layers (MX2; M = Ti, Zr, Hf, Mo, W; X = S, Se, Te) in 1T and 2H structures were screened with Quantum ESPRESSO at the PBE level, recording each calculation’s duration and memory, then supercells up to 3328 electrons and preregistered paired comparisons of no sharing against a job-placing broker. Nine layers have PBE gaps in the 1.0–2.0 eV window of transistor channels and photodetectors, seven after spin–orbit coupling; single-layer 2H cells keep the same nine, and chalcogen-vacancy hop barriers follow the gap, also in Janus layers. In primitive cells and 3×3 supercells, demand followed calculation stage and cell size, which the centre already knows, and no arrangement raised throughput. At 8×8 supercells, compounds of equal electron count differed in memory by 23–32% near node capacity; one disclosed memory-class bit per job raised the centre’s throughput 1.133-fold under memory-reservation charging, but not on single-layer pools, whose memory classes nearly coincide. The group gained no resolvable advantage and job timings revealed the compound, so the hypothesis that the broker benefits both parties was rejected. A gap screen needs batching rather than disclosure; defect and heterostructure supercells justify disclosing one memory class per job.
articles.summary_en: A computational study of transition-metal dichalcogenides found that sharing one memory-demand class can improve computing-centre throughput for large supercell calculations, but provides no measurable benefit to research groups. The authors conclude that batching is preferable for band-gap screening, while limited disclosure may help with defect and heterostructure simulations.

articles.title_original: Surface-dipole contamination of the Schottky-Mott slope: why the Fermi-level pinning factor does not transfer to MXene contacts
articles.title_en: Surface Dipoles Distort Fermi-Level Pinning Analysis in MXene Contacts
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract The pinning factor S = dΦSB/dW is the standard measure of Fermi-level pinning at metal–semiconductor junctions and is increasingly applied to contacts between two-dimensional semiconductors and MXenes. We show that this transfer is not valid. In a metal series W is varied by changing the element; in an MXene series it is varied by changing the surface termination, whose dipole is also the dominant source of deviation from the Schottky–Mott limit. Abscissa and deviation share one origin, and the fitted slope is not a pinning parameter. For the published MoS2/Ti2CT2 data of Gan et al the apparent slope is Sapp = 0.19, conventionally read as strong pinning, although the Ti2CF2 interface obeys the Schottky–Mott rule to within 0.03 eV. The decomposition Sapp = γ + dμIS/dWT, with μIS the interface dipole, resolves the contradiction: the potential discontinuity of 2.50 eV reported by those authors gives a dipole term of −0.79. To measure γ we compute a fixed-termination series of eight metallic F-terminated MXenes on MoS2, which gives γ = 0.87 (95% interval [0.77, 0.96]); the decomposition then returns 0.08 against the observed 0.19, the dipole term accounting for the departure of Sapp from γ to within 20%. An O-terminated series confirms that the dipole stays small at fixed termination. We also re-derive S for every published metal–MoS2 data set from raw barrier heights and document two hazards: at least three distinct quantities are reported as the slope and compared as though interchangeable, and a widely used compilation merges vertical and lateral barriers. A bootstrap test shows that the difference between the frequently quoted experimental S ≈ 0.11 and the first-principles cluster at S ≈ 0.34 is not established at the 95% level.
articles.summary_en: The study shows that Schottky–Mott slopes derived across differently terminated MXenes conflate Fermi-level pinning with termination-induced interface dipoles. Fixed-termination calculations indicate weak pinning at MXene–MoS₂ interfaces, challenging commonly reported interpretations of contact data.

articles.title_original: Selective Functionalization of Graphene Oxide Unlocks Synergistic Catalysis for Organophosphate Degradation
articles.title_en: Site-Selective Graphene Oxide Functionalization Boosts Organophosphate Degradation
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Site-selective functionalization of nanomaterials such as graphene oxide (GO) is a powerful strategy to tailor catalytic performance, with the degree and positioning of functional groups being critical for targeted applications. Herein, we present a systematic study on the functionalization of GO with ethylenediamine through two distinct pathways: (i) attachment at carboxylic acid groups located at the sheet edges and (ii) attachment at epoxide groups distributed across the basal plane. Comprehensive characterization, including XPS, AFM-IR, among others, was consistent with the site-specific functionalization. Importantly, the positioning effect was directly correlated with catalytic activity in the heterogeneous degradation of hazardous organophosphates─compounds widely used in agrochemicals and notorious for their extreme toxicity and persistence in the environment. Our results reveal that functionalization at the epoxide sites, despite yielding a lower degree of modification, produced superior catalytic efficiency, achieving a rate constant of 4.86 min–1 g–1, in contrast to 0.721 min–1 g–1 for the nanocatalyst functionalized via the carboxylic acid. The higher catalytic rate constant was obtained due to synergistic interactions with freely available carboxylic acids acting as intramolecular catalysts. Blocking these carboxylic acids with inert groups led to a marked decrease in activity, emphasizing their mechanistic role. Beyond advancing toward functionalization strategies, this study demonstrates how nanodesign can be leveraged to probe catalytic mechanisms and enhance detoxification of organophosphates. Understanding these synergistic effects in GO-based materials opens new avenues for designing nanocatalysts aimed at mitigating the dual-use hazards of o
articles.summary_en: ACS researchers found that ethylenediamine functionalization at graphene oxide epoxide sites produced substantially higher catalytic activity for degrading hazardous organophosphates than modification at edge carboxylic groups. The findings identify a synergistic catalytic mechanism relevant to graphene-based detoxification materials.

articles.title_original: Synthesis-Controlled Phase Evolution and Implications for the Stability of Ti2CT x MXenes
articles.title_en: Synthesis Optimization Improves Ti2CTx MXene Stability
articles.excerpt_original: MXenes have emerged as a versatile class of two-dimensional materials with exceptional electrical, chemical, and surface properties. However, thinner members, such as Ti2CTx MXene, remain far less explored because of their limited structural stability and high susceptibility to oxidation. In this study, we investigate how excess aluminum during the MAX phase synthesis induces a molten state that governs the formation of the Ti2AlC MAX phase and significantly affects the stability of the resulting Ti2CTx MXene. Excess aluminum promotes more stoichiometric Ti2AlC formation by eliminating residual oxygen and improving powder homogeneity. Quantitative X-ray diffraction phase analysis shows that aluminum content beyond 1.6× progressively increases the fraction of secondary phases, including Ti3AlC2. Adding excess Al produces Al2O3 by eliminating residual oxygen, which may play a crucial role by forming a passive protective layer on the MAX phase to slow etching-reaction kinetics and improve the performance of the resulting Ti2CTx MXene. We identified 1.6 times the stoichiometric aluminum content as the optimal stoichiometric composition for producing the Ti2AlC MAX phase for subsequent MXene synthesis. The optimized 1.6× Al-derived Ti2CTx MXene has a conductivity of approximately 7431 S/cm and exhibits a 75.6% reduction in degradation under ambient conditions compared to the standard 1.2× Al-derived Ti2CTx. Despite these improvements, Ti2CTx MXene remains intrinsically more prone to oxidation than Ti3C2Tx due to the absence of the additional electron-donating Ti layer. These findings highlight the importance of alternative synthesis strategies, such as molten-salt etching, to enable the practical use of thinner Ti2CTx MXenes in applications that require oxidation resistance.
articles.summary_en: Researchers found that using 1.6 times the stoichiometric aluminum content during Ti2AlC MAX-phase synthesis produced Ti2CTx MXene with approximately 7,431 S/cm conductivity and 75.6% lower ambient degradation than material made with 1.2× aluminum. The findings clarify how phase composition and protective Al2O3 formation affect oxidation resistance in this thin MXene.

articles.title_original: Quantum Oscillations across Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene
articles.title_en: Quantum Oscillations Reveal Possible Hole Crystallization in Rhombohedral Graphene
articles.excerpt_original: Recent quantum-oscillation measurements in rhombohedral graphene reveal an abrupt increase in the dominant frequency and the emergence of additional frequencies as the carrier density is lowered toward superconductivity. Noninteracting band models can account for multiple frequencies but do not explain the upward jump. We show that these features can arise from two competing fates of the inner hole pocket in an annular Fermi sea: collapse into a simply connected Fermi liquid or crystallization into an anticrystal, in which localized holes coexist with itinerant electrons. Pocket collapse contracts the outer Fermi contour at fixed density, whereas hole crystallization preserves a larger contour that supports magnetic-breakdown orbits. This contrast provides a possible explanation for the frequency jump, while additional reconstructed orbits produce a multitone spectrum. Our results support the anticrystal as a candidate normal state near superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.
articles.summary_en: Theoretical analysis explains unusual quantum-oscillation frequency jumps near superconductivity through competing hole-pocket collapse and crystallization into an “anticrystal” state. The findings identify a possible normal state and reconstructed magnetic-breakdown orbits in rhombohedral graphene.

articles.title_original: A Mxene-Reinforced Chitosan-Gelatin Adhesive “Brick-and-Mud” System Inspired by Nacre for Fire-Resistant High-Performance Wood Composites
articles.title_en: MXene-reinforced bioadhesive improves fire resistance of wood composites
articles.excerpt_original: Abstract Inspired by the “brick-and-mud” structure of nacre, this study successfully prepared a biomass-based composite adhesive, GMCS@MXene, through a biomimetic design strategy. The material features rigid MXene nanosheets as the “bricks” and a flexible chitosan-gelatin hybrid network as the “mud”, constructing a multilevel structure with excellent interfacial compatibility via a three-step synthesis method. The incorporation of only 0.8 wt % MXene resulted in a synergistic enhancement of multiple performance metrics. Unlike conventional polymer-MXene blends that rely on simple physical mixing, this nacre-mimetic “brick-and-mud” architecture achieves a previously unattainable balance between ultralow filler loading and high flame-retardant efficiency. Compared to the unmodified system, the plywood exhibited substantially improved shear strength, achieved a V-0 classification in the UL-94 vertical burning test, and demonstrated an increased limiting oxygen index of 28.8%. Furthermore, total smoke production was reduced by 68.2%. Mechanistic investigation elucidated the dual role of MXene during combustion. On the one hand, MXene catalyzed the polymer matrix to form a compact and protective char layer. On the other hand, thermal oxidation of MXene generated nanoparticles that became embedded within the char layer, thereby reinforcing its structural integrity and enhancing its barrier properties. This work proposes a plausible dual flame-retardant pathway of MXene featuring promoted carbonization and nanoscale char reinforcement, while also providing insights for developing formaldehyde-free, inherently flame-retardant, eco-friendly wood adhesives.
articles.summary_en: Researchers developed a nacre-inspired chitosan–gelatin adhesive reinforced with 0.8 wt% MXene for plywood. The composite improved shear strength, achieved UL-94 V-0 performance, raised the limiting oxygen index to 28.8%, and reduced total smoke production by 68.2%.
